previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with a history of coronary artery disease and prior stent placement, was admitted for escalating chest pain radiating to the neck and jaw, accompanied by dyspnea, sweating, and nausea. He had not been taking his cardiac medications, including Plavix and aspirin, for about a month. Initial evaluation showed no acute heart attack, but an echocardiogram revealed new regional wall motion abnormalities, raising concern for possible stent occlusion. His pain resolved with medical therapy. During admission, he disclosed ongoing heroin use and experienced withdrawal symptoms, for which he received clonidine and Ativan. Despite recommendations to remain for detox placement, he chose to self-discharge to seek treatment independently. He was discharged home with a full medication refill, follow-up instructions, and referrals for addiction and housing support.
